qa.question: What is a reasonable and normal rent increase in SF 94122 under local, state and federal law?
qa.answer: Local (controls here): the SF Rent Board allowable increase is 1.6% for increases effective March 1, 2026 - February 28, 2027, once per 12 months, on base rent. State: AB 1482's cap (8.8% for the SF region, Aug 1, 2026 - Jul 31, 2027) does NOT apply because these units are already under the lower local cap. Federal: there is no federal rent cap; federal law (Fair Housing Act) governs discrimination only. So a normal, defensible increase is up to 1.6% per year.

qa.question: How do big real estate corporations handle increases vs individual owners in SF?
qa.answer: The same SF Rent Ordinance (Admin Code Ch. 37) applies to both: same annual allowable percentage, same 12-month rule, same notice and license requirements. Corporate ownership changes nothing for these pre-1979 units; it only matters for AB 1482 exemptions on single-family homes/condos, which do not apply here.

qa.question: What is the correct way to inform tenants, and what are reasonable reasons?
qa.answer: Obtain the rent increase license (report units to the Rent Board Housing Inventory) BEFORE imposing an increase. Give written notice: 30 days for increases of 10% or less, 90 days if more than 10% (alone or combined in the same year); add 5 days if mailed. Use the percentage in effect on the effective date. The lawful reason is the annual allowable increase (and any properly banked amounts); anything above the cap requires a Rent Board petition (e.g., approved capital improvements).

qa.question: Can the increase pass review by SF tenant advocates and free tenant lawyers?
qa.answer: Yes if it complies with Ch. 37: within the published allowable percentage, once per 12 months, proper written notice, and a valid rent increase license. An increase that does not conform to the ordinance is null and void; violations can be misdemeanors with a mandatory $1,000 fine. Tenants can get free help: SF Rent Board counseling (415) 252-4600 and the Eviction Defense Collaborative / Right to Counsel (415) 659-9184.

qa.question: Raise one unit's rent or both, to avoid discrimination claims?
qa.answer: No law requires raising both units. But applying the SAME lawful percentage and procedure to all tenants in the building is the defensible, non-discriminatory practice. SF, state (FEHA) and federal (FHA) fair-housing laws prohibit treating tenants differently based on protected classes (race, national origin, familial status, disability, sex, source of income, etc.). Uniform treatment avoids disparate-treatment exposure.
